display.text: A display using separate bars whose heights represent category counts or percentages, making comparisons across categories easy.
The categories of a variable together with the count or proportion of observations in each category.
An estimate of an event's probability obtained by dividing its observed number of occurrences by the total number of trials or observations. Also called relative-frequency probability.
Outcomes that have the same probability of occurring; equal likelihood must be justified by the chance model, not assumed merely because outcomes can be listed.
For a finite sample space with equally likely outcomes, P(A) equals the number of outcomes in event A divided by the total number in the sample space.
A set of outcomes from a sample space satisfying a stated condition; an event occurs when the observed outcome is in that set.
The number of observations belonging to a particular category or exhibiting a specified outcome. Also called category count.
A listing of the categories of a variable and the number of observations in each category.

As a chance experiment is repeated independently under the same conditions, an event's relative frequency approaches its true probability in the long run. This does not require steady improvement after every trial.
One possible result of a random experiment; the experiment's definition determines whether different orders count as different results.
A proportion multiplied by 100, expressing a category's share of the total per hundred observations.
A circular display whose sectors represent categories, with each sector occupying the category's proportion of the whole.
A listing of categories with their frequencies divided by the total count, showing each category's share of the observations. Also called proportional distribution.
